effect: The player's snap legislative election (callSnapElection, aS with cause "player") now obeys the guards the game already applies to AI governments (j1C): no dissolution within 365 days of the chamber's last election (K1C, reason recent_mandate) or within 180 days of its next scheduled election (b1C, reason term_ending). As for the AI, a caretaker government (none formed) is judged on time in caretaker status instead: it may dissolve once it has been caretaker for 60 days (y1C), whatever the mandate or term, and not before (reason formation_pending), so a hung parliament can still be sent back to the voters but a fresh collapse cannot be used to skip the mandate guard. Caretaker time is measured exactly as for the AI: the AI's monthly country review (YJQ, run from the country-operations pass T6C on each country's hashed day of the month) records the government id and the day it first sees caretaker status, and clears the record when the status ends; the player's country is skipped by that review (it runs only for countries the player does not govern), so on the same day the patch keeps the same record for it, as geobalCaretakerWatch on the country. A caretaker government not yet seen by a review counts 0 days, as for the AI, so the wait is 60 days from the first review that sees it (up to about a month after the status starts). A successful player dissolution clears the record (third edit, as YJQ clears the AI's after its dissolution), so if the vote leaves the government caretaker the 60 days start again from the next review instead of allowing another dissolution the next day. Mandate dates come from the chamber's contest, as the AI reads them (T1C): the next election day, and the last election as that day minus the chamber's term (o5), the same day count as the AI's. The one difference: the game's calendar helper (Fg) floors dates at the start of the game, so T1C reads every pre-game election as held on day 0 and the AI never dissolves for advantage in a game's first year; for an election before day 0 the patch counts the days the other way (today plus one term, minus the next election day), so a government elected 18 months before the game starts may call an early election at once. The game's constitutions already record cooldownDays: 365 on the dissolve power, which nothing enforced. A refusal leaves approval unchanged and sends the game's existing snap_election_rejected notice with the reason in its payload; the game has one text for that notice, about the freeze after an electoral reform, and it is kept. Unchanged: the constitutional dissolve power and reform-freeze checks, the -3 approval cost, dissolutions after a lost confidence vote (cause no_confidence) and AI dissolutions (deadlock, opportunity). Not included: a campaign period between dissolution and the vote (the vote is still computed the same day). Real-world behaviour: early elections right after a mandate or just before a term ends are rare and often constitutionally barred. State: geobalCaretakerWatch ({governmentId, sinceDay}) on the player's country while its government is caretaker; absent in old saves (a caretaker government then counts from the next monthly review). Day 0 unchanged (no caretaker government at the start; player action only). (Minified names in this text are those of build 26318758.)
